bug_semantics: When pam_winbind mkhomedir is enabled, _pam_mkhomedir() takes the target account's pw_dir from getpwnam() and, after _pam_create_homedir() treats an already-existing path as success, _pam_chown_homedir() chowns that path with no check that it is not a critical system directory. Accounts whose home is '/' (a common default for nobody and other system accounts) therefore have '/' reowned when a PAM session is opened as that account — by root su or by a non-root user with a narrow sudo run-as-that-account grant — breaking sshd StrictModes, sudo, and package-manager ownership checks. On RHEL '/' ships mode 0555, so the impact is availability loss rather than write privilege escalation.
flaw_origin: The surviving vulnerable control flow was first written in 042df7f0b78d60a721fa35c42e950774261cea1d (2008-08-14, Günther Deschner, 'pam_winbind: re-add mkhomedir option'), which added _pam_create_homedir/_pam_chown_homedir/_pam_mkhomedir so that any successful create — including stat() success on an already-existing directory — is followed by chown(pw_dir, uid, gid) with no path allowlist. A 2006-era create_homedir path (removed in ca09263d00c7c5493f4ab7214c7cfb2cf8a28eea) returned early without chown when the directory already existed and is not the surviving sink. The 2020 TOCTOU refactor fd364b01e2defb5f48238db64d3ef7f6d828c517 switched mkdir-first/EEXIST but kept chown-on-existing-dir.

Red Hat Bugzilla 2499991 and access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-15779 confirm the pam_winbind mkhomedir chown-of-existing-pw_dir mechanism, CWE-732, CVSS 6.1, discovery by Runar Lundgren (Red Hat); live reproduction on samba 4.19.x/4.23.x; RHEL 9.9/10.3 (samba 4.24.3) not affected because chown then fires only on newly created directories.

Advisory line anchors: samba-4.23.5 nsswitch/pam_winbind.c:1622 _pam_chown_homedir() unconditionally chown(dirname); _pam_mkhomedir() at 1662-1666 calls _pam_create_homedir(pw_dir) then always _pam_chown_homedir(pw_dir). _pam_create_homedir treats mkdir EEXIST + S_ISDIR as PAM_SUCCESS, so existing '/' is chowned.

git log -L :_pam_chown_homedir:nsswitch/pam_winbind.c samba-4.23.5 has a single first-write: 042df7f0b78d60a721fa35c42e950774261cea1d (single parent d9efd52fd09af752b3b7fae2a88a522e05e7f672, not a merge/squash). Parent tree source3/nsswitch/pam_winbind.c exists and has no _pam_chown_homedir/_pam_mkhomedir and no chown() calls.

BIC patch at source3/nsswitch/pam_winbind.c (later moved unchanged in 6821d898d7ecf10c6a9359560c5cf1c50a812b62) added _pam_create_homedir that returns PAM_SUCCESS when stat(dirname)==0, then _pam_mkhomedir chowns pwd->pw_dir on that success — the first surviving write of chown-existing-homedir including '/'.

Pre-2006 implementation at ca09263d00c7c5493f4ab7214c7cfb2cf8a28eea^ returned PAM_SUCCESS without chown when directory_exist(pw_dir); that safer code was deleted in 2006 and is not the 4.19/4.23 sink. 6a2d15f1de9fb7b93a31129139dea667303393db is a later v3-3-only re-add, not an ancestor of samba-4.23.5.
2020 fd364b01e2defb5f48238db64d3ef7f6d828c517 (CID 242274 TOCTOU) changed create to mkdir-first/EEXIST but left the caller chown-on-success path intact.

reasoning: The CVE is a published Red Hat CNA record of a real pam_winbind availability flaw, not a withdrawn/rejected advisory. The attack path is mkhomedir=yes plus a PAM session for an account whose pw_dir is '/', causing an unvalidated chown of the filesystem root. git log -L and parent-tree inspection place the first surviving write of that chown-existing-homedir sequence at 042df7f0b78d60a721fa35c42e950774261cea1d; the 2008 commit is a new implementation (always chown after create-success), not a revert of the 2006-era code that skipped chown when the directory already existed, and not the 2008 nsswitch path move. Later TOCTOU and explicit-PAM_SUCCESS edits did not introduce the sink. The 2026 Metzmacher commit on master, and its v4-23/v4-24 cherry-picks, close the sink by chowning only directories mkdir actually created, matching Red Hat's observation that 4.24.3 is unaffected. AI attribution is judged only from that 2008 BIC commit object: human Samba maintainer authorship with no AI/co-author/tool trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
